bib.title: S-LoRA: Serving Thousands of Concurrent LoRA Adapters
bib.venue: MLSys 2024 (Proceedings of the 5th MLSys Conference); arXiv v3 5 Jun 2024

read.skipped: Reference list (lines ~1335-1660) skimmed only; figure plots (Figs 5-12) have no extractable values.

question: How can one machine serve thousands of LoRA adapters of a single base LLM concurrently with high throughput?
hypothesis: Computing xAB on the fly while batching the shared base xW across adapters beats merging adapters into the base weights when many adapters are served.
contributions: Unified Paging: unified memory pool for adapter weights and KV cache
Heterogeneous batching: custom CUDA kernels for varying ranks on non-contiguous memory
S-LoRA TP: tensor parallelism strategy with minimal LoRA communication

method.summary: S-LoRA keeps all adapters in host memory, fetches the adapters needed by the running batch into a unified GPU page pool shared with the KV cache (page = vector of size H), and computes base xW batched via GEMM plus per-adapter xAB with custom kernels (MBGMM prefill in Triton, MBGMV decode adapted from Punica). Built on LightLLM with iteration-level scheduling, adapter prefetching, early-abort admission control and Megatron-aligned tensor parallelism.

other.peft: server batching single-adapter requests, switching adapters between batches

limits: Evaluated only on Llama models and LoRA; other adapter types left as future work.
vLLM-packed baseline is a merged-weights multi-process setup, not real LoRA serving, so the 4x gain is vs a weak baseline.
Table 3 gives no counts between 5 and 100 adapters, so the vLLM OOM threshold is not located; PEFT not run beyond 100 adapters.
Single run per configuration, no variance reported; request-rate per Table 3 row not stated.
Merge ablation measured only on A10G with 1-5 adapters; reported as plot only.
Real workload has ~26 adapters only; thousands tested on synthetic traces.
No accuracy/quality evaluation; adapters are synthetic ranks, not trained.
Future work: more adapter methods, fused kernels, multiple CUDA streams.
